audit_findings.title: Convertible-note and warrant ceiling does not match the earnings claim
audit_findings.magnitude: 7.960680 million excess shares; 21.1% of the stated 37.722 million denominator. Removing them produces 29.761320 million shares and, with unchanged equity values, $18.58 bear, $23.92 base, and $26.48 bull value per share versus $14.66, $18.87, and $20.90
audit_findings.mechanism: The error directly inflates fully diluted shares. At all stated scenario values, the shares are worth far less than the $87.93 conversion price and $135.28 warrant strike, so neither full note-underlying shares nor full warrant shares belong in the denominator; note interest already remains in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, we will settle the principal amount of the 2030 Convertible Notes in cash, and any conversion premium in excess of the principal amount in cash, or a combination of cash and shares of common stock, at our election.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated claim-matching error, not merely a possible risk. Principal must be cash-settled, only an in-the-money premium can create note dilution, warrants require strike-price proceeds, and the hedge offsets note conversion economics above the conversion price. The 26.7% increase in per-share values after removing the unsupported shares is material even though the corrected bull value remains below the $31.03 market price.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the denominator separately for each scenario using contractual net-share settlement, treasury-stock treatment of warrant proceeds, and the hedge. Retain note interest only while the notes remain debt and include shares only for scenario-specific net dilution above the applicable strikes.

audit_findings.title: Dealer floorplan guarantees create a correlated claim far beyond the recorded reserve
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,777.7 million filed contingent liability and $1.3 million filed accrual at May 30, 2026; realized loss unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Dealer defaults would require cash repurchases and any shortfall between repurchase cost and resale proceeds would reduce OE, liquidity, and potentially the equity bridge during a cyclical downturn.
audit_findings.evidence: The total contingent liability on all repurchase agreements was approximately $ 1,640.0 million and $ 1,673.7 million as of August 30, 2025 and August 31, 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual exposure is demonstrated and equals approximately 2.5 times the $712 million base equity value, but it is not equivalent to an expected loss because WGO receives inventory with resale value. The filing does not quantify loss under a correlated dealer-default and resale-price shock. Given the exposure's size and its tendency to crystallize when OE is weakest, it is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Run explicit stresses using dealer and lender concentrations, inventory age, contractual repurchase prices, default rates, resale timing and haircuts, carrying costs, and available liquidity. Deduct the probability-weighted loss or present a separate downside scenario rather than treating the $1.3 million accrual as the only exposure.

audit_findings.title: Cash added to equity may not be distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum identified bridge overstatement of $57.1 million, equal to $1.51 per stated diluted share and 8.0% of the $712 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash dollar-for-dollar to equity value even though operating, seasonal, covenant, debt-service, and contingent-liability needs may require some or all of it.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to satisfy our short-term and long-term obligations through a combination of cash on hand, funds generated from operations, and the borrowing capacity available under our ABL Credit Facility and other debt instruments.
audit_findings.explanation: The full $57.1 million addition is demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much cash is excess. Cash declined by $116.9 million during the latest nine months while the company funded working capital, dividends, and debt reduction, supporting the need for a minimum-liquidity analysis. The possible adjustment is meaningful, but its actual amount and therefore its materiality remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Determine normalized minimum cash from monthly working-capital seasonality, near-term commitments, covenant and borrowing-base headroom, dealer-repurchase stress, dividends, and debt service; rerun the bridge using only cash demonstrably above that requirement.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize an unusually favorable tax year
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed effective tax rates were 14.5% in FY2025, 22.7% in FY2023, and 21.9% for the latest nine months of FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Discrete tax benefits embedded in after-tax FY2025 earnings enter the $46.6 million OE anchor and are then compounded and capitalized throughout the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our effective tax rate decreased to 14.5 % in Fiscal 2025 compared to 66.2 % in Fiscal 2024 primarily due to the prior year's non-deductible debt inducement loss and non-deductible goodwill impairment and, in Fiscal 2025, increased favorable return to provision adjustments and reduced change in the valuation allowance over lower pre-tax income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that favorable return-to-provision adjustments and tax credits reduced FY2025 tax expense, but it does not disclose the portion embedded in owner earnings or the normalized cash tax rate applicable to recurring OE. The direction is downward if the anchor perpetuates nonrecurring benefits, but the available record cannot establish the valuation magnitude.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 book tax, cash tax, credits, valuation-allowance movements, and return-to-provision adjustments. Remove discrete items, calculate recurring pre-tax OE, apply a supportable long-run cash tax rate, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring debt-repurchase loss may be permanently embedded in the trough anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.0 million pretax charge, equal to 4.3% of the $46.6 million anchor; a full $2.0 million anchor addback would increase value by at most approximately $21.3 million bear, $28.1 million base, and $31.4 million bull, or $0.56, $0.75, and $0.83 per stated diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: If unadjusted, the one-time loss reduces after-tax OE and is capitalized as though it recurs indefinitely.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the Senior Secured Notes Tender Offer, we recorded a loss on note repurchase of $ 2.0 million in the accompanying Consolidated Statements of Income during the second quarter of Fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The $2.0 million nonrecurring charge is demonstrated, but its omission from the OE reconciliation is only a possibility. Even using the conservative upper bound of adding back the entire pretax amount without a tax reduction, the corrected bull value would remain about $21.73 per share, well below the $31.03 market price. The isolated finding therefore cannot change the current valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE reconciliation and add back the after-tax loss if it was not already removed. Review the separate $2.9 million restructuring and $1.2 million impairment charges independently for recurrence before making any additional adjustment.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may escape owner-earnings maintenance costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.6 million FY2025 finance-lease principal payments, equal to 3.4% of the $46.6 million anchor; deducting the full amount would reduce value by approximately $17.0 million bear, $22.5 million base, and $25.1 million bull, or $0.45, $0.60, and $0.67 per stated diluted share. Filed finance-lease liabilities were $8.1 million at August 30, 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back finance-lease asset depreciation without deducting principal or an equivalent replacement-capital charge overstates OE. The $450 million bridge debt figure also excludes finance-lease liabilities, although bridge debt is context-only and therefore does not itself change calculated equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Financing leases are primarily for real estate and solar energy producing equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether principal was omitted from the OE calculation is unresolved. The filing establishes $1.2 million of finance-lease depreciation and $1.6 million of principal payments for FY2025. Even assuming the entire $1.6 million was omitted and recurring, the maximum computed valuation reduction is under $0.67 per share and cannot bridge the gap between the $20.90 bull value and the $31.03 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace finance-lease depreciation and principal through the OE reconciliation. If depreciation was added back, deduct the associated principal or a supported replacement-capital amount; also disclose the $8.1 million finance-lease liability alongside other debt context.
